lesson.title: Regression
intro: Regression is used to model the relationship between two variables.
A regression equation predicts a value of y based on a given value of x.
The slope of the regression line describes how y changes as x increases.
Regression models are commonly used for prediction and identifying trends in data.

example.problem: A regression equation is \(y = 3x + 2\). What is the predicted value of \(y\) when \(x = 5\)?
steps: Substitute the value of x into the regression equation.
Simplify to find the predicted value.

questions.prompt: A student finds the regression equation \(y = 2.4x + 5.1\), where \(x\) represents hours studied and \(y\) represents the predicted test score. What is the predicted test score when a student studies \(6\) hours?
The regression equation for a set of data is \(y = -3.2x + 48\). Which statement best describes the relationship between \(x\) and \(y\)?
questions.explanation: The slope of the regression equation is negative (−3.2), which indicates a negative correlation between the variables.

questions.prompt: The regression equation relating temperature \(x\) and ice cream sales \(y\) is \(y = 15x - 120\). What is the predicted number of sales when the temperature is \(10^\circ C\)?
The regression equation for a set of data is \(y = 1.5x + 2\). What is the predicted value of \(y\) when \(x = 6\)?
